title: StreamLink: typed output adapters and stream-first ergonomics for Python SDK
creator: Ayesha Khan
description:
Problem: Users building streaming integrations with Redwood's Python SDK frequently write fragile ad-hoc parsers to map incremental token/chunk events into typed application models (Pydantic/dataclasses). These ad-hoc solutions duplicate retry/parse-state handling, fail to provide clear backpressure behavior, and are awkward to use with the SDK's async iterator streaming surface.

Goal: Deliver a small, composable helper (StreamLink) that provides a clear abstraction for turning streaming responses into typed models with: incremental parse state, idempotent retry boundaries, backpressure hooks, first-class pydantic and dataclass adapters, and ergonomic examples for common patterns (chat messages, structured JSON blobs, event streams).

Why different from existing work: Prior tickets focused on strict schema hydration and streaming-safe builders. StreamLink focuses on the developer ergonomics of "attach a typed parser to a stream" while baking in retry safety, cancellation, zero-copy where possible, and clear backpressure semantics so product teams can adopt streaming typed schemas with minimal boilerplate.
acceptance_criteria:
1) StreamLink exposes an async iterator and an awaitable "map(schema)" helper that yields validated Pydantic or dataclass instances as chunks are completed.
2) StreamLink preserves parse state across transient retriable errors and provides a documented resume protocol for idempotent retries.
3) Backpressure: consumer can set .max_buffer_tokens or provide a backpressure callback to pause upstream batching (documented example).
4) Performance: end-to-end benchmark for a typical chat stream (avg seq_len 512) shows <5% overhead vs raw async iterator processing.
5) API examples (notebook + README) demonstrating chat streaming, JSON-lines streaming, and event-sourcing patterns included.
6) Unit tests cover pydantic adapter, dataclass adapter, retry resume, cancellation, and memory-leak checks.
7) API reviewed and approved by SDK and Runtime owners; PR merged and docs published in SDK reference.
design_decisions:
- Expose a lightweight StreamLink wrapper implementing __aiter__ to be used in for-await loops; provide two convenience helpers: .map_to_pydantic(model) and .map_to_dataclass(cls).
- Parsing model: stream parser will use an incremental buffer and a deterministic completion predicate per schema (user-provided or default: newline-delimited JSON or bracket-matching).
- Retry semantics: StreamLink will tag parse 'checkpoints' at item-completion boundaries. When a retry returns a new stream, resume from last checkpoint rather than replaying partial tokens. This requires cooperation with retry controller in SDK; we'll use the existing retry token metadata header to match requests.
- Backpressure: implement a simple token budget that the consumer can query; if budget exhausted StreamLink will raise BackpressureSignal which the SDK runtime can use to briefly stop pulling from the GPU queue. This is intentionally conservative (pause-on-overflow) rather than complex token-level flow control in first iteration.
- Adapters: use pydantic v2 compatible instantiation path plus a dataclass adapter that supports from_dict and strict-type conversion. Keep adapters pluggable for future third-party validators (attrs, marshmallow).
- Memory: where payloads are bytes, prefer memoryview slices to avoid copying when assembling JSON payloads.
- API ergonomics: sync and async convenience helpers for non-async users (sync generator powered by asyncio loop.run_in_executor internally).
implementation_notes:
Files to add: sdk/python/redwood/streamlink.py (core impl), sdk/python/redwood/adapters/pydantic_adapter.py, sdk/python/redwood/adapters/dataclass_adapter.py, sdk/python/tests/test_streamlink_*.py, examples/python/streamlink_examples.ipynb.
Key PRs: GHPR-Redwood/sdks#742 (core impl), GHPR-Redwood/sdks#743 (adapters + tests), GHPR-Redwood/docs#121 (docs + examples).
Runtime integration: Add a small capability flag in the service response metadata to surface 'pause_on_backpressure' support; if runtime doesn't support it, StreamLink will fall back to local buffering and emit a warning.
Telemetry: emit metrics for average buffer size, checkpoint count, and resume_rate to the SDK telemetry namespace for the feature flag 'streamlink'.
progress_updates: 2025-11-18: Ticket created after spike by SDK team showing repeated patterns across three customers; initial API sketch reviewed in engineering sync.
2025-11-19: Spike complete—prototype streamlink wrapper that maps newline-delimited JSON to pydantic models; measured baseline overhead ~3.2% with simple parser.
2025-11-21: Design review with Runtime team. Agreed on 'checkpoint at item boundary' approach and a lightweight token-budget backpressure signal. Runtime to add optional response metadata flag.
2025-11-22: Started core implementation (streamlink.py). Added unit tests scaffolding and pydantic adapter. WIP PR opened GHPR-Redwood/sdks#742.
2025-11-24: Benchmarks run on dev infra against model shim; found memory copy hotspot in the incremental join—optimizing to use memoryview reduces peak RSS by ~18%.
2025-11-25: Second pass addressing review feedback; adding dataclass adapter and notebook examples. Preparing for internal SDK review by 2025-11-28.
